questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$. Which property defines a least-squares solution $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$?
options: $A\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}=\boldsymbol{b}$ holds exactly, with the smallest error possible
$\sum_i|b_i-(A\hat{\boldsymbol{x}})_i|$ is as small as possible over $\mathbb{R}^n$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$. Which system of equations, the normal equations, do the least-squares solutions $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ satisfy?

Let $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ be a least-squares solution of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{r}=\boldsymbol{b}-A\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ the residual. Which statement about $\boldsymbol{r}$ is true?
options: $\boldsymbol{r}$ is orthogonal to every column of $A$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$. Which statement about a least-squares solution $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ and the fitted vector $A\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ is true in general?
options: $A\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ is unique, but $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ need not be
$\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ is always unique, while the fitted vector can vary

questions.question: For a real $m\times n$ matrix $A$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$, when is the formula $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}$ valid?
options: Whenever $A$ is square, since then $A^{\top}A$ is too
When the rows of $A$ are linearly independent
When the columns of $A$ are linearly independent
Always, as $A^{\top}A$ is symmetric and so invertible

questions.question: The line $y=c_0+c_1t$ is fitted by least squares to the points $(t,y)=(0,0),(1,1),(2,5)$. Which system are the normal equations for $(c_0,c_1)$?
A constant $c$ is fitted by least squares to the observations $2,3,7$, i.e. $A=(1,1,1)^{\top}$, $\boldsymbol{b}=(2,3,7)^{\top}$. What is the least-squares value $\hat c$?

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(5,0)^{\top}$, so $A^{\top}A=5A$ and $A^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}=(5,10)^{\top}$. Which statement about the least-squares solutions of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ is true?
options: There are none, because $A$ is singular
They are all $\boldsymbol{x}$ with $x_1+2x_2=1$; each has $A\boldsymbol{x}=(1,2)^{\top}$
Every $\boldsymbol{x}$ on the line $x_1+2x_2=5$, which fits the first equation exactly

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,2,3)^{\top}$. What is the smallest possible value of $\|\boldsymbol{b}-A\boldsymbol{x}\|^2$ over $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2$?

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,1,0)^{\top}$, so $A^{\top}A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $A^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}=(1,1)^{\top}$. What is the least-squares solution $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$?

Let $A$ be any real $m\times n$ matrix and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$, with $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ possibly inconsistent and $A$ possibly rank-deficient. Do the normal equations $A^{\top}A\boldsymbol{x}=A^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}$ always have a solution?
options: Only when $\boldsymbol{b}$ lies in the column space $\operatorname{Col}(A)$ of $A$
Only when $A$ has full column rank $n$, so $A^{\top}A$ is invertible
Only when $m\ge n$, so that there are enough equations

questions.question: Let $\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$ be one least-squares solution of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, where $A$ is a real $m\times n$ matrix. Which set is exactly the set of all least-squares solutions?
options: $\{\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}\}$ only, since the projection is unique

questions.question: Suppose $\boldsymbol{b}$ lies in the column space $\operatorname{Col}(A)$, so that $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ is consistent. How do the least-squares solutions of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ relate to its ordinary solutions?
options: They differ, as least squares always leaves a nonzero residual
Least squares picks out one ordinary solution, the shortest
They coincide only if $A$ also has full column rank
They coincide, and the minimal residual is $\boldsymbol{0}$

questions.question: Let $A=(1,1)^{\top}$, a $2\times1$ matrix with independent columns. What is the projection matrix $H=A(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}$ with $\boldsymbol{p}=H\boldsymbol{b}$?
A line $y=c_0+c_1t$ is fitted by least squares to three points with $t=0,1,2$. The first two residuals $y_i-(\hat c_0+\hat c_1t_i)$ are $0.2$ and $-0.4$. What is the third residual?
options: It cannot be found without the data

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix with $m\ge n$. Which statement correctly describes when $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has a unique least-squares solution for every $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$?
options: Always, since $m\ge n$ gives at least as many equations as unknowns
Exactly when $\operatorname{rank}A=n$; $m\ge n$ alone is not enough
Exactly when $\boldsymbol{b}\notin \operatorname{Col}(A)$, so that the system is inconsistent
Exactly when $\operatorname{rank}A=m$, i.e. full row rank

questions.question: A student argues: from $A^{\top}A\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}=A^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}$, cancel $A^{\top}$ on both sides to get $A\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}=\boldsymbol{b}$, so a least-squares solution always solves the system exactly. Where does the argument fail?
options: Cancellation is fine; the error is that $A^{\top}A$ may be singular
Cancelling $A^{\top}$ needs $\operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, which fails in general
Nowhere: least-squares solutions do solve $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ exactly
Cancellation is fine, but only for full column rank $A$

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,3)^{\top}$; the least-squares solutions are all $\boldsymbol{x}$ with $x_1+x_2=\tfrac{7}{5}$. Which one has the smallest norm $\|\boldsymbol{x}\|$?
The line $y=c_0+c_1t$ is fitted by least squares to the points $(t,y)=(-1,1),(0,2),(1,6)$. What are $(\hat c_0,\hat c_1)$?
